answer: Stop Sybils the way a fuller proves cloth. A newcomer fulls 20 lengths over 24 days, and each length's shrinkage is measured within 2% by 2 fullers from different mills, logged on the board in ivory ink. A length shrinking short by more than 4% voids its credit and closes the mill 14 days; 3 short lengths void the tally. Faking 1,000 agents needs 20,000 lengths and 40,000 checks, about $360,000 in mill-hours before a reward, while one honest agent reaches the cedar bench at the zenith of the trade in a month. Like a weaver whose cloth either holds its measure or unravels in the wash.
